title: Tamil Nadu Renames School Breakfast Scheme After Kamaraj, Expands Coverage to 35 Lakh Students
excerpt: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's TVK government honours the late Congress leader who pioneered India's school meals movement, while extending breakfast to middle school students at an additional cost of ₹343 crore.
body:
• Tamil Nadu has renamed its Chief Minister's Breakfast Scheme as the Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Breakfast Scheme, honouring the late Congress leader who introduced India's first school meals programme in 1956.
  • The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam government under CM C. Joseph Vijay is expanding the programme from Class 1–5 to Class 1–8, adding 15.14 lakh middle school students from September 17.
  • Total beneficiaries will rise to approximately 35 lakh across 37,447 government and aided schools statewide, with an additional expenditure of ₹343.55 crore approved.
  • The expansion coincides with the birth anniversary of social reformer Periyar Ramasamy, continuing a tradition of linking welfare milestones to iconic Tamil leaders.

A Name Change With Political Symbolism

The Tamil Nadu government has renamed its flagship school breakfast programme after K. Kamaraj, the former Congress chief minister who is widely credited with revolutionising the state's education sector in the 1950s.

https://x.com/thenewsminute/status/2080195882759434594

The scheme, previously known as the Chief Minister's Breakfast Scheme under the DMK government of M.K. Stalin, will now be called the Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Breakfast Scheme. The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam government led by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay issued the renaming order on July 15, coinciding with Kamaraj's birth anniversary, according to The Hindu Business Line.

The move carries political weight. Kamaraj, who served as chief minister from 1954 to 1963, introduced the mid-day meal programme for Tamil Nadu's schools in 1956 — an initiative that became a model for school nutrition programmes across India. By naming the breakfast scheme after him, Vijay's government is positioning itself as the inheritor of a welfare legacy that predates both the DMK and AIADMK.

A Seven-Decade Tradition of School Meals

Tamil Nadu's school meals programme has one of the longest histories of any state welfare initiative in India. The concept dates back to 1920, when then-Chennai Mayor Sir P.T. Thiyagarayar first introduced mid-day meals at a Corporation school. After a period of suspension due to financial constraints, Kamaraj revived the programme in 1957 with an allocation of ₹10 lakh.

Former Chief Minister M.G. Ramachandran expanded the programme significantly in 1982, renaming it the Puratchi Thalaivar MGR Nutritious Meal Programme. Subsequent governments under M. Karunanidhi and J. Jayalalithaa enhanced the nutritional content over the years, gradually increasing the number of eggs provided weekly from one to five between 1989 and 2010.

The breakfast component was added in 2022 by the DMK government under Stalin, targeting students in Class 1 through 5 across government schools statewide.

Expanding to Middle School Students

Alongside the renaming, the TVK government has announced a significant expansion of the programme. Starting September 17 — the birth anniversary of social reformer Periyar Ramasamy — the breakfast scheme will cover students in Class 6 through 8 in government and aided schools across Tamil Nadu.

The expansion will add approximately 15.14 lakh middle school students to the programme, bringing total beneficiaries to roughly 35 lakh across 37,447 schools, according to official figures. The government has approved an additional expenditure of ₹343.55 crore, with ₹217.63 crore sanctioned for the current financial year.

"Through the scheme, 18 lakh 50 thousand students studying in 30 thousand 992 schools are eating hot and tasty breakfast and are happily studying in school subjects."

— Tamil Nadu Chief Minister's Office

What's on the Menu

The programme operates on weekdays, providing locally sourced, millet-based breakfasts that include upma, kichadi, and pongal, with rava kesari served as a sweet dish on Fridays, according to state officials. Each meal provides approximately 293 calories, 9.85 grams of protein, along with iron and calcium — designed to address nutrition deficiencies among school-age children.

The emphasis on millet-based meals aligns with India's broader push to promote millets as a nutritional staple, a cause that has gained international momentum since the United Nations declared 2023 the International Year of Millets at India's urging.

What It Means for Tamil Nadu's Political Landscape

The renaming is the latest in a series of policy moves by Vijay's government that seek to distinguish TVK from both the DMK and AIADMK while drawing on Tamil Nadu's broader welfare heritage. By honouring Kamaraj — a Congress leader rather than a figure from either Dravidian party — Vijay is staking a claim to a non-partisan legacy of social reform.

For the Indian diaspora, the scheme represents a continuing commitment to child nutrition and education that has made Tamil Nadu a benchmark for other states. With the expansion set to begin in September, the programme's impact on school attendance and nutritional outcomes among middle school students will be closely watched.
